title: audit-proxy-mini-sdk-prd-rough
content:
Summary:
A tiny first-party SDK ("mini audit proxy") that customers running Redwood Private can drop into their edge/operator stack to: 1) emit compact, signed audit events to the customer-configured audit forwarder, and 2) provide lightweight local validation hooks for approval decisions. The goal is a minimal integration surface (Python + Go), deterministic event shape, and optional cryptographic envelope for tamper-evidence when customers choose it.

Problem we solve:
- Private deployments need a low-friction way to capture and ship small proof artifacts (change intent, approval decision, endpoint metadata) without shipping full-blown log agents or heavy SIEM integrations.
- Customer operators want a predictable schema and stable library so app teams don't copy/paste ad-hoc payloads that break auditability.
- Ops needs sampling/edge-filtering primitives to avoid sending full payloads for very high-volume control-plane events.

Product assumptions / constraints:
- Targets customer-managed environments (on-prem, VPC) where installing a new agent is sometimes blocked; SDK must be embeddable within existing control plane components.
- First release: Python + Go packages since those cover most operator tooling and customers' onboarding scripts.
- Optional crypto (HMAC + KMS-backed signing) is a v1+ feature but SDK must support pluggable signing hooks.
- Not a replacement for bulk SIEM forwarders. Focus on control-plane change events, approval traces, and small forensic snapshots.

Success criteria (90 days):
- Working prototype with example integration in ops/orchestration repo (demo that sends 3 event types).
- Documented event schema and sample receiver config (syslog/HTTP).
- Two pilot customers onboarded and an internal red-team test for tamper detection.

Primary personas:
- Customer platform engineer (integrates SDK into onboarding scripts and operator agents).
- Customer security/audit analyst (consumes compact events in their SIEM).
- Redwood solutions engineer (helps debug, validates evidence during onboarding).

Core event types (minimal set):
- change_request: {id, actor, target, diff_summary, timestamp, request_origin}
- approval_decision: {id, change_id, decider, outcome, policy_ref, timestamp}
- evidence_snapshot: {id, change_id, artifact_type, compressed_blob_ref, hash, timestamp}
(we will publish canonical JSON schema; SDK emits these fields plus an envelope header)

API sketch (developer UX):
- Python (pseudo):
  from redwood_audit import AuditClient
  c = AuditClient(destination_url=..., signer=KMSHook(...), sampling_policy="qps:10")
  c.emit_change_request(...)
  c.emit_approval_decision(...)
  # optional local validate hook
  ok = c.validate_approval_signature(signed_payload)

Integration checklist (for onboarding playbook):
- choose transport: HTTP to customer forwarder OR local unix socket for agent pickup
- install package and import into control-plane component
- configure sampling and batching (defaults: batch window 2s, max 50 events)
- configure signer: none | local HMAC key | KMS-backed key reference
- wire up health endpoint + basic metrics (events_emitted, events_dropped, last_send_error)

Telemetry and observability requirements:
- SDK exposes metrics via Prometheus client: audit_events_total{type="..."}, audit_events_dropped_total{reason="..."}, audit_send_latency_ms_bucket
- Tracing: optional W3C traceparent propagation to tie SDK emits to request traces
- Local debug mode: human-readable event dumps to stdout for devs

Sampling and volume control model:
- Local policy language (tiny): "sample if rate>n OR always for approvals where outcome=denied"
- Default conservative sampling: 1/100 for change_request; always send approval_decision and evidence_snapshot when present
- Edge deduplication: ephemeral dedupe window 30s based on change_id

Security / signing / KMS notes:
- Signing is pluggable. SDK will support an interface for signing hooks.
- Customers can supply HMAC key or call out to their KMS/HSM via a provided hook (examples for AWS KMS, GCP KMS).
- Signed envelope contains signature, signer_id, and public metadata (hash algorithm).
- For tamper detection in early pilots, we will provide a reference verification tool that checks a chain of signed events for inconsistencies.

Receiver considerations (customer side):
- Provide example receiver: small Go HTTP server that validates signature, stores minimal index (change_id => latest decision), and forwards full payloads to SIEM or object store for long-term retention.
- Include sample policies for rejecting unsigned events when customer opts-in.

Operational playbook (pilot):
- Night 0: integration in staging cluster with debug logs enabled, collect metrics for 48h
- Week 1: flip sampling to production rates, validate that SIEM is receiving expected counts, run simulated change storms
- Rollback criteria: >1% of control-plane flows experiencing >5s delay because of SDK blocking or unrecoverable send errors

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- Should SDK buffer to local disk when forwarder is unreachable? (pros: reliability; cons: disk management and retention complexity)
- Strict signing by default? increases onboarding friction for small customers. Recommend opt-in for first pilots.
- Canonical compression format for evidence_snapshot blobs (zstd vs gzip) — prefer zstd by default but need C bindings for small footprints.
- Will we publish a test-suite that customers can run locally to validate compatible receiver behavior? (yes, high priority)

Backward compatibility / versioning plan:
- v0.1: experimental. Event shapes explicit in README. No backwards compatibility guarantee.
- v0.2: schema version field added; SDK will include basic migration helpers.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Customers incorrectly configure sampling and lose critical evidence. Mitigation: ship conservative defaults and explicit onboarding checklist with policy templates.
- Risk: SDK becomes operationally heavy (disk retention etc.). Mitigation: keep initial feature scope minimal; extra storage features in v1+ only.

Prototype tasks (engineering):
- produce Python & Go packages with the emit API + basic HTTP transport (2 engineers, 3 sprints)
- example receiver service + verification tool (1 engineer, 2 sprints)
- docs and sample configs + internal demo (1 tech writer, 1 sprint)
- privacy/security review + legal signoff for signing recommendations (1 sprint)

Next steps (this doc):
- Sync with Solutions Eng (Diego) to identify 2 pilot customers that can accept early SDK installs
- Align with Security (Priya) on recommended signing hook patterns and sample code for AWS KMS
- Kick off a 6-week prototype sprint (owners listed above)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Keep payload schema minimal — fewer fields -> easier customer adoption
- Consider a tiny CLI (audit-proxyctl) for operators to replay and validate event chains locally
- We should avoid building a separate storage service; prefer to integrate with customer object store or SIEM

TODOs:
- [ ] finalize canonical JSON schema and publish as schema.json in repo
- [ ] implement HMAC signer example
- [ ] write receiver example for Splunk/Elastic ingestion patterns
- [ ] draft pilot onboarding email + checklist
